truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

The volume of a cone is given by \(V_C=\pi r^2 h\), where \(r\) is the radius of the circular base and \(h\) is the height of the cone.

Using the values given:

\(V_C = {@float(rad)@}^2 \pi \times {@float(height)@}\)

\(V_C = {@decimalplaces(V_C,5)@}...\)

\(V_C = {@decimalplaces(V_C,3)@}cm^3\) (to 3dp)


The volume of a sphere is given by \(V_S=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3\), where \(r\) is the radius of the sphere.

Therefore, the volume of hemisphere is given by \(V_S=\frac{2}{3} \pi r^3\)

Using the values given:

\(V_{HS} = \frac{2}{3} \pi \times {@float(rad)@}^3\)

\(V_{HS} = {@decimalplaces(V_HS,5)@}...\)

\(V_{HS} = {@decimalplaces(V_HS,3)@}cm^3\) (to 3dp)


The total volume of the ice cream is given by the sum of the volumes of the cone and hemisphere.

\(V_T = V_C + V_{HS}\)

\(V_T = {@decimalplaces(V_C,5)@}... + \ {@decimalplaces(V_HS,5)@}...\)

\(V_T = {@decimalplaces(V_T,3)@}cm^3\) (to 3dp)

truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

The curved surface area of a cone is given by \(A_C=\pi r l\), where \(r\) is the radius of the circular base and \(l\) is the slanted length along the surface of the cone.

Using Pythagoras' Theorem:

\(l^2 = r^2 + h^2\)

\(l = \sqrt{{@float(rad)@}^2 + {@float(height)@}^2}\)

\(l = \sqrt{{@float(rad^2+height^2)@}}\)

Therefore:

\(A_C = {@float(rad)@} \pi \times \sqrt{{@float(rad^2+height^2)@}}\)

\(A_C = {@decimalplaces(A_C,5)@}...\)

\(A_C = {@decimalplaces(A_C,3)@}cm^2\) (to 3dp)


The surface area of a sphere is given by \(A_S=4 \pi r^2\), where \(r\) is the radius of the sphere.

Therefore, the curved volume of hemisphere is given by \(A_S=2 \pi r^2\)

Using the values given:

\(A_{HS} = 2 \pi \times {@float(rad)@}^2\)

\(A_{HS} = {@decimalplaces(A_HS,5)@}...\)

\(A_{HS} = {@decimalplaces(A_HS,3)@}cm^2\) (to 3dp)


The total surface area of the ice cream is given by the sum of the surface areas of the cone and hemisphere.

\(A_T = A_C + A_{HS}\)

\(A_T = {@decimalplaces(A_C,5)@}... + \ {@decimalplaces(A_HS,5)@}...\)

\(A_T = {@decimalplaces(A_T,3)@}cm^2\) (to 3dp)
